pairs.question: quid semper loquimurne, sodales, nil agimus? regem interimi numquid iuvat ipsum? en vobis hic certa manus.
pairs.answer: iamdudum hoc agimus, Perci, nobis ut agamus dignum aliquid, factis praeeant sed verba necesse est, cernendis veluti debentur lumina rebus. perdere tam multa sibi prole superstite regem, res non digna satis tanta fortissime dextra est.
pairs.derivation: Percius bursts in and asks his fellow plotters a genuine interrogative (numquid iuvat regem ipsum interimi?), faulting their inaction (nil agimus?). Dropped the interleaved speech tag 'ait' to keep the utterance contiguous; the marginal verse number 170 is stripped. Catisbaeus replies ('sic excipit illum ore Catisbaeus blaeso, tamen ad mala prompto:' narration stripped): I begin the answer at 'iamdudum hoc agimus, Perci' (answers 'nil agimus?') and include the next sentence 'perdere tam multa... dextra est' which answers whether killing the king alone is worthwhile (no, not a worthy deed while his offspring survive). Cut at the full stop after 'dextra est'; the next sentence ('ad maiora tibi vigeat dum provocat usus...') turns from answering to elaborating his own grander scheme. Stripped the marginal verse numbers 175 from within the answer span.
